mainTopic: Which widows and converts' daughters a כהן may marry, whether parents are believed about a child's status (יכיר), and the start of the משנה about a father and his agent betrothing his daughter.
overview: The amud opens by finishing רבא's reading of the פסוק in יחזקאל about widows. Its first half is about a כהן גדול and its second half is about a regular כהן. He proves that a פסוק can switch subjects like this from the פסוק about שמואל lying 'in the היכל'. The גמרא then explains that 'מכהן יקחו' means the rest of the כהנים may marry a widow. רבי יהודה disagrees: a כהן may marry only the widow of a man whose daughter could marry a כהן, which fits his strict view about a convert's daughter. The הלכה follows רבי יוסי, who says even the daughter of two converts may marry a כהן. In practice we advise against such a marriage ahead of time, but we do not break it up once it has happened. Next comes a new משנה: parents are not believed to call their child a ממזר, but רבי יהודה says they are, based on the word 'יכיר' about a בכור. The גמרא then works out what 'יכיר' teaches according to the חכמים. The amud ends with the start of a משנה about a father and his agent who both betroth his daughter, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Can one verse switch from a High Priest to a regular priest?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן is surprised by רבא's reading: the start of the פסוק is about a כהן גדול and the end is about a כהן הדיוט.
steps.simpleTranslation: This verse: the first part is about a כהן גדול and the last part is about a regular כהן?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן pushes back on רבא's earlier reading of the פסוק in יחזקאל. He finds it strange that one פסוק would talk about two different people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא needed this split so the פסוק would not contradict itself, since one half bans a widow and the other half allows one. רב נחמן is asking whether it makes sense to split one פסוק between two subjects with no sign of the change. The question is about how a פסוק can be read, not about the הלכה itself.

phrases.english: This verse,
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק in יחזקאל 44:22 that רבא just explained.

phrases.english: its first part is about a High Priest
and its last part is about a regular priest?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי קְרָא, רֵישָׁא בְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל וְסֵיפָא בְּכֹהֵן הֶדְיוֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's reading of the פסוק from the earlier part of the daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading that splits the פסוק between a כהן גדול and a כהן הדיוט.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It seems unlikely that one continuous פסוק changes its subject in the middle without saying so.

steps.title: רבא stands by his reading
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers simply: yes, that is how the פסוק should be read.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא confirms that he really does mean to split the פסוק between two kinds of כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not back down or change his reading. His short 'yes' sets up the next question, which asks whether a פסוק can really be written this way.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's surprised question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, the first part is about a כהן גדול and the last part is about a כהן הדיוט.

steps.title: Is any verse actually written this way?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן presses further: does the תנ״ך ever write a פסוק like that?
steps.simpleTranslation: And is a verse ever written like that?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן asks for an example. Is there any other פסוק that switches subjects in the middle?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the challenge is about how פסוקים work in general. If רבא cannot point to a similar case, his reading looks forced. This sets up רבא's proof in the next step.

phrases.english: And is a verse written like this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on רבא's 'yes' and asks for a real example.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a פסוק can split between two subjects.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without another example of a פסוק like this, the split reading has no support.

steps.title: Proof from שמואל sleeping 'in the Sanctuary'
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings the פסוק about שמואל lying in the היכל. It must be split, because only kings from בית דוד may even sit in the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, as it is written: 'And the lamp of God had not yet gone out, and שמואל was lying in the Sanctuary of ה׳.' But only kings of בית דוד may sit in the עזרה! Rather, read it like this: 'the lamp of God had not yet gone out' in the Sanctuary of ה׳, and 'שמואל was lying' in his own place.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא proves that פסוקים can switch subjects in the middle. He points to a פסוק that we are forced to split into two parts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read straight through, the פסוק says שמואל lay down inside the היכל. That cannot be, because nobody except a king from בית דוד may even sit in the עזרה, let alone lie down there. So the words 'in the Sanctuary of ה׳' go with the lamp, and שמואל was lying somewhere else. A פסוק split in this way is exactly the kind of example רב נחמן asked for.

keyTerms.meaning: The lamp of God, the מנורה

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a general rule for reading פסוקים: when the plain flow of a פסוק leads to something impossible, we may split it into separate parts that have different subjects.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes, as it is written:
"And the lamp of God had not yet gone out,
and Shmuel was lying in the Sanctuary of ה׳" —
phrases.notes: שמואל א 3:3

phrases.english: but isn't it true that there is no sitting in the Temple courtyard
except for the kings of the house of David alone!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: ״נֵר אֱלֹהִים טֶרֶם יִכְבֶּה״ – בְּהֵיכַל ה׳,
phrases.english: Rather: "the lamp of God had not yet gone out" in the Sanctuary of ה׳,
"and Shmuel was lying" in his own place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's request for an example of a split פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That one פסוק can talk about two different subjects without any marker.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל א 3:3. It must be split, because only kings of בית דוד may sit in the עזרה.
steps.whatToRemember: A פסוק can switch subjects partway through. Just as the פסוק about שמואל is split, the פסוק in יחזקאל can be split between a כהן גדול and a כהן הדיוט.

steps.title: Only a priest's widow, not an Israelite's?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves on to the words 'אלמנה מכהן יקחו'. Read simply, they suggest a כהן may marry only a כהן's widow, which is not the הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the widow who is a widow of a כהן they may take.' A כהן's widow, yes, but a ישראל's widow, no?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks at the second half of the פסוק in יחזקאל. It points out that the simple reading seems to limit which widows a כהן may marry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'מכהן' describes the widow's late husband, then a regular כהן could marry only the widow of another כהן. But the הלכה is that a כהן הדיוט may marry any widow. So this reading must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Of a כהן, or from among the כהנים
A regular Jew who is not a כהן or לוי

phrases.english: "And the widow who is a widow
of a priest, they may take" —
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 44:22

phrases.english: "of a priest" yes, but of an Israelite no?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having settled the split, the גמרא now looks closely at the wording of the second half.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain meaning of 'אלמנה מכהן יקחו'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read simply, the words seem to forbid a כהן הדיוט from marrying a ישראל's widow, which goes against the accepted halacha.

steps.title: 'Of a priest' means the other priests may marry her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'מכהן' describes the men who marry. The rest of the כהנים, meaning everyone except the כהן גדול, may marry a widow.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: 'מכהן יקחו': the rest of the כהנים may take a widow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by moving the word 'מכהן' from the widow over to the men doing the marrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מכהן' is not telling us whose widow she is. It tells us who may marry her: 'from among the כהנים', meaning every כהן other than the כהן גדול. This fits רבא's split: the כהן גדול may not marry a widow, but the other כהנים may marry any widow.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is saying

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'מכהן' as 'the widow of a כהן'. Here it means 'from among the כהנים', and it describes who is allowed to marry her.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
"Of a priest they may take": from the rest of the priests, they may take.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about 'מכהן'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading a word: 'מכהן' describes the men who marry, not the widow's late husband.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words seemed to allow only a כהן's widow.
steps.terutzMaskana: All כהנים other than the כהן גדול may marry any widow.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the same thing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא backs up the explanation that 'מכהן יקחו' means the rest of the כהנים may marry a widow.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: 'מכהן יקחו' means the rest of the כהנים may take.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the very same reading, which supports what it just said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in the last step was not just the גמרא's own idea. An earlier source, a ברייתא, read the פסוק the same way. This support from a תנא makes the reading stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
"Of a priest they may take": from the rest of the priests, they may take.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer from the previous step.
steps.raayaObject: That 'מכהן יקחו' means 'the rest of the כהנים may take'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that reads the פסוק the same way.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's different reading
steps.stepSummary: In the same ברייתא, רבי יהודה reads the פסוק differently: a כהן may marry the widow only of a man whose daughters may marry into כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: they may take a widow from those who marry off their daughters to כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes on with a second opinion. רבי יהודה reads 'מכהן' as being about the widow's late husband after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the words limit which widows are allowed. The late husband must be someone whose daughter could marry a כהן. A man whose daughter may not marry a כהן leaves a widow that a כהן may not marry either.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who marry off their daughters to כהנים

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
From those who marry off to the priesthood, they may take.
phrases.notes: He means men who can marry off their daughters to כהנים. The words 'their daughters' are understood, not written.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: מִן הַמַּשִּׂיאִים לַכְּהוּנָּה יִקָּחוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא quoted in step 7, giving רבי יהודה's dissenting reading of 'מכהן יקחו'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן may marry only the widow of a man whose daughter is allowed to marry a כהן.

steps.title: רבי יהודה follows his own view about a convert's daughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי יהודה's reading fits his known view: a male convert's daughter is like a male חלל's daughter, and a widow follows the same rule as a daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה follows his own reasoning, for he said: the daughter of a male convert is like the daughter of a male חלל. Anyone whose daughter you may marry, you may marry his widow. Anyone whose daughter you may not marry, you may not marry his widow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יהודה reads the פסוק this way. It ties his reading to a view he holds elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that a male convert's daughter may not marry a כהן, just like a חלל's daughter. He also holds that a man's widow follows the same rule as his daughter. So a כהן may not marry a convert's widow, and the פסוק teaches this through the words 'מכהן יקחו'.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning, consistent with his view elsewhere
A man born from a forbidden priestly union, who is not fit for כהונה

steps.whatToRemember: There are two readings of 'מכהן יקחו'. The ברייתא says it means all כהנים except the כהן גדול may marry any widow. רבי יהודה says a כהן may marry only the widow of a man whose daughter could marry a כהן, which leaves out a convert's widow.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda follows his own reasoning, as he said:

phrases.aramaic: בַּת גֵּר זָכָר כְּבַת חָלָל זָכָר,
phrases.english: The daughter of a male convert is like the daughter of a male ḥalal,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה's view from earlier in the פרק. Just like a חלל's daughter, a convert's daughter may not marry a כהן.

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאַתָּה נוֹשֵׂא בִּתּוֹ – אַתָּה נוֹשֵׂא אַלְמְנָתוֹ,
phrases.english: anyone whose daughter you may marry, you may marry his widow,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁאִי אַתָּה נוֹשֵׂא בִּתּוֹ – אִי אַתָּה נוֹשֵׂא אַלְמְנָתוֹ.
phrases.english: and anyone whose daughter you may not marry, you may not marry his widow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רבי יהודה's reading by linking it to his view elsewhere.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A widow follows the same rule as the daughter. Since a convert's daughter is not allowed to a כהן, a convert's widow is not allowed to a כהן either.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי from the משנה: even the daughter of a male convert who married a female convert may marry a כהן. Two אמוראים rule that the halacha follows him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: even when a male convert married a female convert, their daughter may marry a כהן. רב המנונא in the name of עולא, and רבה בר בר חנה, both say the halacha follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי יוסי's opinion in the משנה and gives the ruling: the הלכה follows him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה says a male convert's daughter may not marry a כהן at all. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב allows her only if one of her parents was born Jewish. רבי יוסי is the most lenient: even the daughter of two converts may marry a כהן. Two separate אמוראים agree that this is the הלכה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Even a male convert who married a female convert.
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the משנה. He means that their daughter may still marry a כהן.

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna said in the name of Ulla:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yosei.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה:
phrases.english: And so too Rabba bar bar Chana said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from רבי יהודה's view to the last opinion in the משנה and gives the ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The daughter of two converts may marry a כהן. The halacha follows רבי יוסי.

steps.title: Priests took on a stricter practice after the Temple's destruction
steps.stepSummary: After the בית המקדש was destroyed, כהנים chose to be strict for themselves, following רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the time the בית המקדש was destroyed, the כהנים held themselves to a higher standard and followed רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds that even though the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, the כהנים took on a stricter custom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a custom of extra care, not a change in the הלכה. The כהנים acted like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and avoided marrying a convert's daughter unless one parent was born Jewish.

keyTerms.meaning: Extra care, holding oneself to a higher standard

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the הלכה changed to follow רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. The הלכה is still like רבי יוסי. The כהנים simply chose to be stricter for themselves.

phrases.english: And from the day the Beis Hamikdash was destroyed
the kohanim practiced a higher standard for themselves
like Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov.
phrases.notes: In the משנה, he holds that a convert's daughter is fit only if one of her parents was born Jewish.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִיּוֹם שֶׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ נָהֲגוּ כֹּהֲנִים סִילְסוּל בְּעַצְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a stricter custom on top of the ruling in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, כהנים were strict like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

steps.title: Before marriage we advise strictness; after marriage we do not separate
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא combines both opinions. If a כהן asks ahead of time, we tell him to follow רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. If he already married her, we follow רבי יוסי and leave the marriage alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said that רב הונא told him: if a כהן comes to ask first, we instruct him like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. If he already married her, we do not take her away from him, because we follow רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical bottom line. Which opinion we follow depends on whether the marriage has already happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the marriage, we can easily follow the stricter custom, so we do. After the marriage, the real הלכה is like רבי יוסי, so there is no basis to break up the couple.

keyTerms.meaning: He comes to ask advice beforehand

steps.whatToRemember: The daughter of two converts may marry a כהן, as רבי יוסי says. Ahead of time we advise against it, as רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says. If the marriage already happened, it stays.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic pattern in הלכה. We are stricter before something is done (לכתחילה) and accept it once it is done (בדיעבד).

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן, אָמַר לִי הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: Huna told me:
If he comes to ask beforehand, we instruct him
phrases.notes: "He" is a כהן asking whether he may marry the daughter of two converts.

phrases.english: like Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov;
if he already married her, we do not take her away from him,
like Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings together the halacha (step 10) and the custom (step 11) into one practical rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Before the marriage, advise strictly like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. After the marriage, follow רבי יוסי and do not separate them.

steps.title: New משנה: a parent is not believed to call a child a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: A father who says his son is a ממזר is not believed. Even both parents together are not believed about a fetus, but רבי יהודה says they are.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says 'This son of mine is a ממזר,' he is not believed. Even if both parents admit that the fetus in her womb is a ממזר, they are not believed. רבי יהודה says they are believed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It deals with whether parents are believed when they say their own child is a ממזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion says parents cannot make their child a ממזר just by saying so. This is true even when both parents agree, and even about an unborn child. רבי יהודה disagrees and believes them.

keyTerms.meaning: A child born from a forbidden union, who may not marry into the Jewish community

phrases.english: Mishnah
One who says "This son of mine is a mamzer"
is not believed.
And even if both of them admit
phrases.notes: "Both of them" means the father and the mother.

phrases.english: about the fetus in her womb that it is a mamzer,
they are not believed.
Rabbi Yehuda says: They are believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאוֹמֵר בְּנִי זֶה מַמְזֵר אֵינוֹ נֶאֱמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: parents' believability about their child's ייחוס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the first opinion, parents are not believed to make their child a ממזר, even both together and even about a fetus. רבי יהודה says they are believed.

steps.title: What do the words 'and even both of them' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what new point the משנה teaches with the words 'and even both of them.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'and even both of them' mean? What does it add?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the wording of the משנה. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'even' suggests the second case is a bigger point than the first. The גמרא wants to know exactly what makes the case of both parents and a fetus a bigger point than the case of the father alone.

phrases.english: Gemara
What is "and even both of them"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a phrase in the משנה from step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra point is taught by 'and even both of them' beyond the father's case?

steps.title: First point: even the mother, who knows for sure, is not believed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה uses a 'not only... but even' style. Not only is the father not believed, since he cannot be sure who the father is. Even the mother, who does know, is not believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is speaking in a 'not only... but even' way. Not only is he not believed, since he cannot be certain. Even she, who is certain, is not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. It gives the first new point hidden in 'and even both of them.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man can never be completely sure a child is his, so it makes sense that he is not believed. The mother does know the truth, and you might think she should be believed. The משנה teaches that even she is not believed.

keyTerms.meaning: It goes without saying (not only... but even)
It is clear to him, he knows for sure

phrases.english: It is saying "not only... but even":
Not only him,
since it is not clear to him,
phrases.notes: A father cannot be fully sure the child is really his.

phrases.english: but even her, for whom it is clear,
she is not believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Both of them' adds that even the mother, who knows the truth, is not believed.

steps.title: Second point: even about a fetus, who has no presumed status yet
steps.stepSummary: Not only are the parents not believed about a born child, who is already presumed fit. They are not believed even about a fetus, who has no presumed status yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: Not only where the child already has a presumption of being fit are they not believed. Even about a fetus, which has no such presumption, they are not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its answer. It gives the second new point: the case of a fetus.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A child who is already born is presumed to be fit (חזקת כשרות), and that makes it harder to believe the parents against him. A fetus does not have that presumption yet, so you might think the parents should be believed. The משנה teaches that they still are not.

keyTerms.meaning: A presumption of being fit (of proper lineage)

steps.whatToRemember: 'And even both of them' teaches two extra points. Even the mother, who knows for sure, is not believed. And even about a fetus, who has no presumed status yet, the parents are not believed.

phrases.english: And not only where
he has a presumption of being fit
are they not believed,
but even about a fetus as well,
which has no presumption of being fit,
phrases.notes: A fetus has no set status yet because it hasn't been born.

phrases.english: they are not believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא מִיבַּעְיָא הֵיכָא דְּאִית לֵיהּ חֲזָקָה דְכַשְׁרוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the second point in answer to step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'And even' also teaches that the parents are not believed even about a fetus, who has no presumption of being fit.

steps.title: The source for רבי יהודה: the word 'יכיר'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה from the משנה and brings a ברייתא showing his source: the פסוק 'יכיר' means a father is believed to say who his בכור is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says the parents are believed. This matches a ברייתא: 'He shall acknowledge' means he must make the בכור known to others. From here רבי יהודה said: a person is believed to say, 'This is my firstborn son.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי יהודה's words in the משנה and shows the פסוק his view is built on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says the father 'יכיר' (shall acknowledge) the בכור, and the ברייתא reads this as 'he makes him known to others.' So a father's word alone is trusted about which son is the בכור. This is the base on which רבי יהודה builds his wider rule in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
He makes him known to others

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: They are believed.
As it is taught: 'He shall acknowledge' means he shall make him known to others.
phrases.notes: דברים 21:17

phrases.english: From here Rabbi Yehuda said:
A person is believed to say: 'This is my firstborn son.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי יהודה's view in the משנה (step 13) and gives its source.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's view that parents are believed about a child's status
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא reading 'יכיר' (דברים 21:17) as 'make him known to others'

steps.title: רבי יהודה extends the rule to a son with a flawed status, and the חכמים disagree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that just as a father is believed about a בכור, he is believed to say his son is a בן גרושה or a בן חלוצה. The חכמים say he is not believed about that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as a person is believed to say 'This is my firstborn son,' he is also believed to say 'This is the son of a divorced woman' or 'This is the son of a חלוצה.' The חכמים say: he is not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה takes the father's believability from the בכור case and applies it to saying his son has a flawed status. The חכמים reject that extension.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A son of a כהן born from a גרושה or a חלוצה is a חלל and loses the rights of כהונה. רבי יהודה says the father's word counts here too, just like with a בכור. The חכמים limit the father's believability to naming the בכור only.

keyTerms.meaning: Son of a divorced woman (born to a כהן, he is a חלל)
Son of a woman released through חליצה (also flawed for כהונה)

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים here agree that a father is believed about which son is the בכור. They only disagree about believing him that his son has a flawed status.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְשֵׁם שֶׁנֶּאֱמָן אָדָם לוֹמַר: ״זֶה בְּנִי בְּכוֹר״,
phrases.english: And just as a person is believed to say: 'This is my firstborn son,'
so too a person is believed to say
'This is the son of a divorced woman' and 'This is the son of a חלוצה.'
And the Sages say: He is not believed.
phrases.notes: He means not believed about the flawed status. About the בכור, the father is believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא, building on the בכור rule from step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: a father is believed to say his son is a בן גרושה or a בן חלוצה. חכמים: he is not believed.

steps.title: What does 'יכיר' teach according to the חכמים?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק asks רבא: רבי יהודה uses 'יכיר' for his rule, but what do the חכמים learn from it?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said to רבא: It makes sense for רבי יהודה, because that is why 'יכיר' is written. But for the חכמים, why do I need 'יכיר'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the חכמים: if they don't believe the father about status, the word 'יכיר' seems to have no job for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in the תורה must teach something. For רבי יהודה, 'יכיר' gives the father power to identify his sons. The question is what this word adds for the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: That is why it is written

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said to Rava:
It makes sense according to Rabbi Yehuda –
that is why 'he shall acknowledge' is written,
but according to the Rabbis, why do I need 'he shall acknowledge'?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה – הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב ״יַכִּיר״, אֶלָּא לְרַבָּנַן, ״יַכִּיר״ לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the חכמים from step 18 explain the פסוק used in step 17.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the father is not believed about status, the word 'יכיר' seems to teach nothing for them.

steps.title: 'יכיר' is for when nobody knows who the בכור is
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק is needed for a case where the בכור needs to be identified, and the father's word identifies him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for when he needs identifying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for the חכמים: 'יכיר' teaches that the father is believed when it isn't known which son is the בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually everyone knows who was born first, so no one needs the father's word. 'יכיר' is for a case where this is unclear, and then the father's word decides. This is narrower than רבי יהודה's use, since it says nothing about a flawed status.

phrases.english: In a case where he needs identification.
phrases.notes: He means a case where people don't know which son was born first, so the father has to point him out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the פסוק to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'יכיר' has no job for the חכמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: For the חכמים, 'יכיר' teaches that the father is believed when the בכור's identity is unknown.

steps.title: For the double portion, the father is believed anyway because of מיגו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which law this is about. If it is the double portion, we don't need a פסוק, since the father could simply give that son the extra share as a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what law? To give him a double portion? That is obvious, so why do I need a פסוק? Since if he wanted, he could give it to him as a gift, wouldn't it be given to him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer: believing the father about the double portion seems to need no פסוק at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בכור gets a double share of the inheritance. But the father could give any son extra property as a gift while alive, so his word should be accepted anyway. This is a מיגו: since he could get the same result another way, we believe what he says.

keyTerms.meaning: A double portion of the inheritance
Since he could have done/claimed something else, we believe him

phrases.english: For what law?
To give him a double portion?
phrases.notes: דברים 21:17

phrases.english: It is obvious, why do I need a verse?
Since if he wanted,
to give it to him as a gift,
wouldn't it be given to him?
phrases.notes: In other words, he could have handed this son the extra share anyway, so why would we need a פסוק to trust him?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאי הִלְכְתָא? לָתֶת לוֹ פִּי שְׁנַיִם? פְּשִׁיטָא, לְמָה לִי קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'יכיר' is needed to believe the father about the בכור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Because of a מיגו (he could give it as a gift), the father would be believed about the double portion even without a פסוק.

steps.title: The פסוק covers property the father gets later
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק is needed for property that comes to the father after he speaks, which he could not have given as a gift, so the מיגו doesn't work.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is about property that came to him later.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק matters for property the father only gets after he identifies the בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person can only give a gift of what he owns now. For property he receives later, the מיגו of 'he could have given it as a gift' does not apply. So the פסוק is needed to give the בכור his double share of that later property based on the father's word.
steps.whatToRemember: For the חכמים, 'יכיר' means the father is believed to identify an unknown בכור. It matters even for property he gets later, where a gift-מיגו can't help. רבי יהודה goes further and believes the father about a flawed status too.

phrases.english: With property that came to him afterward.
phrases.notes: He means after the father identified the בכור. He didn't own it yet, so he couldn't have given it away as a gift then.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case so the מיגו doesn't apply
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father's word needs no פסוק because of the gift מיגו.
steps.terutzMaskana: For property the father gets later, there is no מיגו, so the פסוק is needed.

steps.title: According to רבי מאיר, why is the פסוק needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: according to רבי מאיר, a person can give away something not yet in the world, so the father could gift even future property. Why is ״יַכִּיר״ needed?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי מאיר, who says a person can transfer something that does not exist yet, why do I need ״יַכִּיר״?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 22. That answer said the פסוק is needed for property the father could not give as a gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 said the פסוק is needed for property that came to the father later, because he could not have given it away beforehand. But רבי מאיר holds that a person can give away something that has not come into the world. So the father could have gifted even that future property, the מיגו works again, and the פסוק seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.term: אָדָם מַקְנֶה דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לָעוֹלָם
keyTerms.meaning: A person can transfer something that does not exist yet (רבי מאיר's view)
"He shall acknowledge" (דברים 21:17), the source that a father is believed about which son is the בכור

phrases.english: And according to רבי מאיר,
who says a person can transfer ownership of
something that has not yet come into the world,
phrases.notes: So the father could give away property he will only get later, which brings back the gift argument from step 21.

phrases.english: why do I need "He shall acknowledge"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, דְּאָמַר אָדָם מַקְנֶה דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לָעוֹלָם, ״יַכִּיר״ לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 22 by applying it to רבי מאיר's view
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the פסוק is needed for property that came to the father after he spoke
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי מאיר, future property can also be given as a gift, so the מיגו still works and the פסוק adds nothing.

steps.title: The פסוק covers property that came while the father was dying
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק is needed for property that came to the father when he was a גוסס, when he could not give it away as a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed where the property came to him when he was a גוסס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ״יַכִּיר״ is needed for property that came to the father while he was a גוסס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At that stage the father cannot give away his property as a gift, even according to רבי מאיר. So there is no מיגו, and only the פסוק can make his word count. Even that property is divided with a double share to the son he named as the בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: A person in the final stage before death
"Fell to him": property that came into his possession, for example through inheritance

steps.whatToRemember: Each view on giving away future property leaves a case where the father has no gift argument. For those who say you cannot give away something not yet in the world, it is property that came later. For רבי מאיר, it is property that came while he was a גוסס. In those cases only ״יַכִּיר״ makes his word count.

phrases.english: Where the property came to him when he was on the verge of death.
phrases.notes: At that point he can no longer give property away, so the gift argument does not work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23 by finding a case where even רבי מאיר agrees the father cannot give a gift
steps.terutzHavaAmina: According to רבי מאיר the father can always give a gift, so the פסוק has no use
steps.terutzMaskana: A גוסס cannot give gifts, so for property that came to him then, the פסוק is needed

steps.title: New משנה: a father and his agent both betroth his daughter
steps.stepSummary: A father lets an agent betroth his daughter but also betroths her himself. Whichever betrothal came first is valid. The משנה begins the case where the order is unknown.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who gave permission to his agent to betroth his daughter, and then went and betrothed her himself: if his betrothal came first, his betrothal is valid; if his agent's came first, the agent's betrothal is valid; and if it is not known...
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins about a father and his agent who each betroth the same girl to a different man. The amud ends partway through the third case, and the ruling for that case comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making the agent does not take away the father's own power to betroth his daughter. The rule is simple: the first betrothal takes effect, because after that she is already married. The open question is what to do when no one knows which came first.

keyTerms.meaning: An agent who acts on someone's behalf
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage

steps.confusionAlert: In "וְאִם שֶׁל שְׁלוּחוֹ קָדְמוּ – קִידּוּשָׁיו קִידּוּשִׁין", the word "his" means the agent's betrothal, not the father's.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One who gave permission to his agent
to betroth his daughter,
and he himself went and betrothed her,
phrases.notes: He betrothed her to a different man than the one the agent chose.

phrases.english: if his betrothal came first,
his betrothal is a valid betrothal;
and if his agent's betrothal came first,
his betrothal is a valid betrothal;
phrases.notes: Here "his" means the agent's betrothal.

phrases.english: and if it is not known
phrases.notes: He means it's not known which betrothal came first. The ruling continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מִי שֶׁנָּתַן רְשׁוּת לִשְׁלוּחוֹ לְקַדֵּשׁ אֶת בִּתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of ״יַכִּיר״ ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a father and his agent both betroth his daughter, the first betrothal is valid; the case of unknown order is introduced next.
